term: full ancestor closure and headless coverage characterization
definition: For every supplied graph, each selected node’s full reflexive finite ancestor cone is closed under all incoming edges. Positive predecessor availability at every node is equivalent to every full cone being headless. With explicit excluded middle, absence of any graph source is equivalent to that headless-cone coverage. Self-loops and cycles are allowed; neither infinitude nor a linear distinct-node chain is asserted. Empty graphs satisfy the universal clauses vacuously.
note: One conjunction of universally quantified structural properties. Its no-source equivalence uses explicit excluded middle in the result; the closure and positive-availability clauses are constructive. This does not assume every actual being lacks a cause.
